description.p: nelson.io.zip reads, writes and inspects ZIP archives entry by entry, on disk or in memory, without extracting them to files.

Entries compressed with store, deflate, zstd, xz, bzip2 or lzma are read transparently. Any other compression method (for example deflate64) is an error that names the method and the entry. Reading checks the size and the checksum of each entry. MaxSize protects against entries that expand far beyond what is expected.

Encrypted entries (WinZip AES with 128, 192 or 256-bit keys, or traditional PKWARE encryption) are read with the Password given at opening; the Encrypted variable of entries tells which ones are. The password is used as UTF-8 text. A wrong password raises an error, and a changed AES entry fails its authentication code when it has been read to its end.

An archive opened with mode 'w', 'a' or 'x' and a Password encrypts the files written afterwards by write, add and fopen. Encryption chooses the method: 'aes256' (default), 'aes128' or 'zipcrypto'. 'zipcrypto' is weak: use it only for old tools. Archives encrypted with 'aes192' are read, but writing with 'aes192' raises the error Nelson:io:zip:invalidArgument. Folders are not encrypted. Encryption without Password, or in mode 'r', raises the error Nelson:io:zip:encryptionNeedsPassword. An unknown method raises the error Nelson:io:zip:unknownEncryption. A password that is not text raises the error Nelson:io:zip:invalidTextOption.
open also accepts an http or https URL in mode 'r'. The archive is downloaded to a temporary file, which is deleted by close.
add compresses the files of a folder one after the other and writes them in order.

New entries use deflate unless Compression is given for the archive (at opening) or for one entry. nelson.io.zip.compressions lists the methods of the running build. In the WebAssembly version, only store and deflate are available, and 'zipcrypto' is the only encryption method.

The compression level applies to the whole archive: the first file written sets it. A later entry that asks for another level raises the error Nelson:io:zip:invalidArgument. When needed, give the level once, at opening: nelson.io.zip.open(filename, 'w', 'Level', 9).
Files larger than 4 GB and archives with more than 65535 entries are written in ZIP64 format.
A writer must be closed to be complete: close writes the central directory. tobytes closes an in-memory writer and returns its bytes.

remove and rename rewrite a ZIP file: the entries they keep are decompressed and compressed again. They cannot keep encrypted entries (error). A name ending with '/', or a name matching no entry but used as a folder, applies to every entry under that folder: rename(f, 'old', 'new') turns 'old/a.txt' into 'new/a.txt'.

An archive opened with mode 'a' knows its existing entries: entries lists them, and write or add refuse a name already present. The archive is written again: existing entries are decompressed and compressed again into a temporary file, which replaces the original file at close. An archive with encrypted entries cannot be opened in mode 'a' (error Nelson:io:zip:invalidArgument).
The functions are also methods of nelson.io.ZipArchive: z.read(name) is nelson.io.zip.read(z, name).

fopen opens an entry as a file identifier: the usual file functions read or write it block by block, without loading it in memory. fclose checks the checksum of a read entry and finishes a written one.
Positioning is exact. Moving forward decompresses and skips the data; moving backward in a compressed entry reads it again from its start, which is slow for large entries.

Several entries can be read at the same time. One entry at a time is written: until its identifier is closed, write, add, another fopen for writing and close raise an error. Deleting the archive object closes it when that entry ends, and fclose('all') finishes the entry.
